seoDescription: Learn to build a PHP application from scratch with the Symfony 3 framework. This practical tutorial guides you through creating a simple to-do list with full CRUD functionality. You'll start by setting up your local development environment, including installing the Symfony installer and configuring a virtual host with Apache. Discover the core concepts of the Symfony project structure, including bundles, controllers, and the Twig templating engine. Master annotation-based routing to create clean URLs.

chapters.title: Introduction to Symfony & the Project
chapters.description: An overview of the Symfony PHP framework and the plan to build a simple CRUD to-do list application using Symphony 3.

chapters.title: Installing the Symfony CLI & Fixing the PATH
chapters.description: This chapter covers downloading the Symfony installer, running into a PATH variable issue on Windows, and adding the PHP directory to the environment variables.

chapters.title: Creating a New Symfony 3 Project
chapters.description: After fixing the PATH variable, this chapter shows how to create a new Symfony project from the command line and access the default welcome page in the browser.

chapters.title: Configuring an Apache Virtual Host
chapters.description: Learn how to set up a clean development URL by configuring a virtual host in Apache's vhosts file and updating the local hosts file on Windows.

chapters.title: A Tour of the Symfony Directory Structure
chapters.description: This chapter provides a brief overview of the default Symfony application structure, including the app, resources, views, src, and web directories.

chapters.title: Understanding Annotation-Based Routing
chapters.description: Discover how Symfony uses annotations within controller classes to define application routes, eliminating the need to manually edit a routing configuration file.

chapters.title: Creating the TodoController & Initial Views
chapters.description: This chapter walks through creating a new TodoController, defining a list action, and setting up the corresponding view files for the application's CRUD functionality.

chapters.title: Defining and Testing CRUD Routes & Actions
chapters.description: Build out the controller by adding actions and annotation routes for create, edit, and details, including how to handle URL parameters like an ID.

summary:
## Project Overview
This video series walks through building a simple **CRUD** (Create, Read, Update, Delete) to-do list application using the **Symfony 3** PHP framework.

## Environment Setup

*   **Symfony Installer**: The project is bootstrapped using the official Symfony installer, which is downloaded and executed via a PHP command.
*   **Windows PATH Variable**: A common setup issue on Windows is the `php` command not being recognized. To fix this, add the path to your PHP executable (e.g., `C:\xampp\php`) to the system's `Path` environment variable.

> [!IMPORTANT]
A system reboot is often required for the new `Path` variable to take effect in all command prompts.

*   **Project Creation**: Once the installer is set up, a new application skeleton is generated with the command `php symphony new <project-name>`.

## Local Development Server

*   The public entry point for a Symfony application is the `/web` directory.
*   For development, it's best to configure a virtual host to provide a clean URL.

1.  **Edit `httpd-vhosts.conf`**: In your Apache configuration, create a `<VirtualHost>` block.
2.  **Set `DocumentRoot`**: Point the `DocumentRoot` to your project's `/web` directory (e.g., `C:/xampp/htdocs/todolist/web`).
3.  **Set `ServerName`**: Assign a local domain name (e.g., `todolist`).
4.  **Edit `hosts` file**: In your system's `hosts` file, map the `ServerName` to the loopback IP: `127.0.0.1 todolist`.
5.  **Restart Apache**: Apply the changes by restarting your Apache server.

## Symfony Architecture

*   **`app/`**: Contains application configuration (`config/`), resources like views (`resources/views/`), and caching.
*   **`src/`**: Your PHP source code, organized into **Bundles**.
*   **Bundles**: Reusable, isolated packages of code. The project starts with a default `AppBundle` where we'll place our controllers.
*   **`web/`**: The public document root containing the front controllers (`app.php` for production, `app_dev.php` for development).

## Controllers & Routing

*   **Controllers**: Classes that handle HTTP requests and return responses. They typically extend Symfony's base `Controller` class.
*   **Actions**: Public methods within a controller that correspond to specific pages or endpoints.
*   **Annotation-Based Routing**: Instead of a central routing file, routes are defined directly above action methods using `@Route` annotations.

    ```php
    use Sensio\Bundle\FrameworkExtraBundle\Configuration\Route;

    /**
     * @Route("/todos/edit/{id}", name="todo_edit")
     */
    public function editAction($id)
    {
        // ...
    }
    ```

> [!TIP]
> Route parameters like `{id}` are defined in the annotation and can be passed directly as arguments to the action method.

## Views & Templating

*   Symfony uses the **Twig** template engine by default.
*   Views are standard HTML files with Twig syntax, stored in `app/resources/views/`.
*   It's a best practice to organize views into sub-directories named after their corresponding controller (e.g., `views/todo/`).
*   Render a view from a controller using `$this->render('todo/index.html.twig');`.
